name: Village history board

layers.essential_history: [[c:The village board is called Warmington: A Brief History. It says the village name comes from an Anglo-Saxon leader, and that the settlement was the farm of Wyrma's people. Late in the 7th century the King of Mercia gave the land to the Abbey of Peterborough, and Warmington appears in the Domesday Book.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The board says the village stayed at around 300 people for five centuries, until the bypass opened in 1996 and new building began. The Nene Way across the water meadows leads to Fotheringhay, where Mary, Queen of Scots was executed in 1587. It also mentions The Fern, an ancient woodland shown on a 1621 map, with snowdrops and aconites in late winter and bluebells in spring.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Journal page: ]]Mr Vale[[c:, the steward, keeps the grain accounts and the keys to the stores. Everyone trusts him. Almost everyone.]]
